signals_basics.caption: The smooth blue curve is a continuous-time signal; the gold stems are a discrete-time signal that only exists at the sample instants n/fs. Change fs to see how much of the wave the samples keep.

dirac_delta.caption: A narrow pulse of area 1 approaches the impulse δ(t) and the ramp approaches the unit step u(t); the pulse is the slope of the ramp. Shrink w to see the limit.

lti_properties.caption: A linear system doubles its output when you double the input. Clipping breaks that: once the input exceeds the limit L the output stops following, so the system is no longer linear.

convolution.caption: The output is the pulse smeared by the system's impulse response. A slow system (large T) gives a low, long output; a fast one reproduces the pulse.

fourier_transform_ee.caption: A short pulse (top) has a wide spectrum (bottom); a long pulse has a narrow one. Time and frequency spread are inversely related.

laplace_signals.caption: Each pair of s-plane poles is a damped oscillation e^(-σt) sin(ωt): the real part sets the decay, the imaginary part the ringing. Poles in the left half-plane decay, so the system is stable.

z_transform.caption: In the z-plane a pole at radius r decays like r^n and its angle sets the oscillation per sample. Inside the unit circle the response dies away; push r past 1 and it grows.

aliasing.caption: Above the Nyquist limit fs/2 a fast sine is sampled so sparsely that the samples fit a slower wave (dashed): the alias. Raise the signal frequency past fs/2 and watch the apparent frequency fall.

spectra_filtering.caption: A 3 Hz tone and a 20 Hz tone pass through a low-pass filter. Lower the cutoff below 20 Hz and the high tone shrinks in the waveform and in the spectrum below it.

modulation_basics.caption: Multiplying a low-frequency message by a carrier shifts its spectrum up: the 30 Hz carrier gets sidebands at 30 ± fm. Raise the depth m for stronger sidebands.

dtft_dft.caption: Sampling a 1 s window gives a DFT with bins 1 Hz apart. Each tone shows up as one spectral line at its frequency; move the tones and watch the lines follow.

fft_algorithm.caption: The direct DFT needs N² multiplications; the FFT needs only N log₂N. At N = 1024 that is about a hundred times fewer, and the gap keeps growing.

fir_filters.caption: An M-tap moving average is the simplest FIR low-pass filter. More taps narrow the passband and place nulls at multiples of 1/M.

iir_filters.caption: Feedback lets a two-pole IIR filter resonate. Pushing the pole radius r toward 1 sharpens the peak at the pole angle, something an FIR filter would need many taps to do.

windowing_methods.caption: A tone that does not fit a whole number of cycles in the window leaks across the spectrum, hiding the weak neighbour at f₀+6. A Hann window (w = 1) tames the leakage.

multirate_processing.caption: Decimation keeps every M-th sample of a 64 Hz stream. If the new Nyquist limit 32/M falls below the signal frequency, it aliases, which is why a low-pass filter must come first.

quantization_effects.caption: Rounding to B bits turns a smooth wave into steps. Each extra bit halves the step and adds about 6 dB of signal-to-quantisation-noise ratio.

fixed_vs_float.caption: Fixed point has a constant step, so small numbers lose relative accuracy. Floating point keeps relative error about 6×10⁻⁸ at every size, which is why it is easier but costs more hardware.

dsp_applications.caption: A DSP chain digitises a signal, computes on it as numbers, and converts back. The same pattern serves audio, images, radar and radio.

vector_analysis_em.caption: Divergence measures how much field spreads out of a point (a source); curl measures how much it circulates. Set one to zero and see the pure source or pure swirl.

electrostatics_dielectrics.caption: Between capacitor plates D stays constant, but inside a dielectric the field E drops by 1/εr because the material's dipoles oppose it. Less field for the same charge means more capacitance.

magnetostatics_materials.caption: Iron multiplies the flux density by μr until it saturates near 1.8 T; air stays on the shallow dashed line. A larger μr means the same field needs far less current.

maxwell_equations.caption: A changing E creates B and a changing B creates E, so together they travel as a wave at c. Raise the frequency and the wavelength λ = c/f shrinks.

plane_waves.caption: The tip of the electric field traces a shape as the wave passes. Equal components 90° apart give a circle (circular polarisation); in phase gives a line; anything else an ellipse.

reflection_refraction.caption: Light bends toward the normal entering a denser medium (Snell's law n₁ sinθ₁ = n₂ sinθ₂). Going from dense to less dense at a steep angle it cannot escape and reflects totally.

transmission_lines.caption: A pulse travels down a 50 Ω line and reflects from the load with coefficient Γ = (Z_L − Z₀)/(Z_L + Z₀). A matched 50 Ω load absorbs it; open or short circuits reflect it fully.

standing_waves_vswr.caption: Incident and reflected waves add into a standing pattern. The more reflection, the deeper the nulls and the higher the VSWR = (1+|Γ|)/(1−|Γ|).

smith_chart.caption: The Smith chart maps every impedance z = r + jx onto one disc: circles are constant resistance, arcs constant reactance. Move z and watch the reflection Γ (gold) and its constant-VSWR circle.

impedance_matching.caption: A quarter-wave section of impedance √(Z₀Z_L) cancels the reflection exactly at the design frequency (f/f₀ = 1) and keeps it low over a band around it.

waveguides.caption: Below the cutoff fc = c/2a nothing propagates. Above it the signal speed v_g climbs toward c while the phase velocity exceeds c (their product is c²).

skin_effect.caption: At high frequency AC current crowds near the surface of a conductor and falls by 1/e at the skin depth δ. Slide the frequency up and the copper core stops carrying current.

antenna_fundamentals.caption: The lobe shows how strongly an antenna radiates in each direction. A narrower beam (larger n) puts more power forward: higher directivity, measured against the dashed isotropic reference.

dipole_antennas.caption: A dipole radiates most broadside to its axis (gold) and nothing along it. A half-wave dipole (L = 0.5) gives a smooth doughnut; lengths past one wavelength split the pattern into extra lobes.

antenna_arrays.caption: N antennas fed in step make a narrow beam broadside; shifting their phases steers it electronically. Spacing above one wavelength lets extra grating lobes appear.

emi_emc.caption: Interference needs a source, a coupling path and a victim. Each fix breaks one path: filters stop conducted noise, shields stop radiated noise, careful grounding avoids loops.

crystal_structure_ee.caption: Top view of the silicon diamond lattice: each atom bonds to four neighbours. Colours show the four heights within a cell (white boxes). Stretch the lattice constant to see density fall.

carrier_statistics.caption: f(E) is the probability that a state at energy E is filled. At low temperature it is a sharp step at the Fermi level; heating smears it over a few kT.

pn_junction_physics.caption: Reverse bias widens the depletion region and lowers the junction capacitance C = εA/W; forward bias squeezes it. The lighter-doped side (here 10¹⁶ cm⁻³) takes most of the width.

bjt_physics_deep.caption: Collector current is β times the base current, but it creeps upward with V_CE because the base narrows (the Early effect). The slope sets the output resistance r_o = V_A/I_C.

mosfet_physics_deep.caption: On a log scale the subthreshold region is a straight line: current falls one decade per S millivolts of gate voltage. Physics limits S to kT/q·ln10 ≈ 60 mV/dec at room temperature.

short_channel_effects.caption: As the channel gets shorter the drain starts to steal control from the gate: threshold voltage rolls off, and a high drain voltage lowers it further (DIBL). A smaller λ means better gate control.

optoelectronic_devices.caption: An LED emits photons with energy near the band gap, so the colour is λ = 1240/Eg nm. Wider-gap materials (GaN) glow blue; narrower ones (GaAs) emit infrared.

lasers_semiconductor.caption: Below threshold the diode glows weakly like an LED; above it stimulated emission takes over and power rises steeply. Heat raises the threshold current, so the same drive gives less light.

photodetectors_solar.caption: A solar cell is a photodiode run as a generator: light sets the short-circuit current, the diode sets the open-circuit voltage, and the best power is at the knee. Heat lowers voltage and power.

fabrication_lithography.caption: The smallest printable feature is CD = k₁λ/NA. Shorter wavelengths and larger numerical aperture shrink it; EUV at 13.5 nm prints lines DUV can only reach with multiple exposures.

fabrication_overview.caption: Silicon is purified, grown into a crystal, sliced into wafers, then built up layer by layer (about 80 times) before being cut into chips and packaged.

doping_implantation.caption: Implantation drops dopants in a bell-shaped profile at the projected range Rp (set by ion energy). Annealing makes them diffuse, widening and lowering the peak while the total dose stays 10¹⁴ cm⁻².

oxidation_process.caption: Thermal oxide grows linearly at first (reaction-limited), then more slowly as oxidant must diffuse through the oxide already there (x² + Ax = Bt). Steam (w = 1) grows it much faster than dry O₂.

etching_process.caption: A mask protects the silicon while the etch removes the rest. Isotropic (wet) etching also eats sideways under the mask; anisotropic (plasma) etching goes nearly straight down.

deposition_processes.caption: CVD grows a film continuously at a rate set by gas flow and temperature; atomic layer deposition adds one self-limiting atomic layer per cycle, giving exact thickness control but slower growth.

system_modeling.caption: A series RLC circuit (L = 10 mH, C = 1 µF) has the same equation as a mass on a spring with damper: more resistance means more damping and less overshoot.

block_diagrams_mason.caption: Reduce a feedback loop to one transfer function: C/R = G/(1 + GH). With a large forward gain the loop behaves like 1/H, set by the feedback part alone.

time_domain_specs.caption: Overshoot, peak time, rise time and settling time describe how a response looks. Less damping (small ζ) is faster to rise but overshoots and rings for longer.

routh_hurwitz.caption: For the loop with characteristic equation s³ + 6s² + 11s + 6 + K = 0, Routh's table says the system is stable only for K < 60. Raise K and watch two poles cross the imaginary axis exactly there.

bode_nyquist_margins.caption: For L(s) = K/[s(s+1)(s+10)] the phase reaches −180° at ω = 3.16 rad/s. The gain margin is how far the gain can rise before it equals 0 dB there; a negative margin means the loop is unstable.

lead_lag_compensators.caption: A lead compensator (1+sT)/(1+αTs) adds phase between its zero and pole, buying phase margin at the cost of higher high-frequency gain. Smaller α gives more lead.

state_space.caption: State-space trajectories: each arrow shows how the state (position x₁, velocity x₂) of a mass–spring–damper moves. A damped system spirals into the origin; no damping gives closed loops.

controllability_observability.caption: The states reachable by input B are spanned by B and AB. When these two arrows line up (b = 0) the rank [B AB] drops to 1 and one mode can no longer be steered.

pole_placement.caption: State feedback u = −Kx on a double integrator gives the closed-loop equation s² + k₂s + k₁ = 0. Choose the gains and the poles land exactly where you want.

digital_control.caption: A digital controller only updates every Ts seconds and holds the value between. The staircase is on average half a sample late, which erodes phase margin.

analog_modulation.caption: In FM the message changes the carrier's frequency. A larger modulation index β puts energy into more sidebands (spaced by fm), widening the bandwidth to about 2fm(β+1) (Carson's rule).

digital_modulation.caption: Each dot is one symbol (a bit pattern) as an amplitude and phase. Packing more dots carries more bits per symbol but brings them closer, so less noise is needed to confuse them.

noise_snr_ber.caption: Noise occasionally pushes a symbol across the decision boundary. The bit error rate falls steeply as Eb/N₀ rises, and denser constellations (16-QAM) need about 4 dB more.

information_entropy_capacity.caption: Shannon's limit C = B·log₂(1+S/N): capacity grows with bandwidth but only logarithmically with signal-to-noise ratio. Every 3 dB of SNR buys about one extra bit per hertz at high SNR.

error_correcting_codes.caption: Codewords are spaced a Hamming distance d apart. Any received word within t = ⌊(d−1)/2⌋ errors of one codeword snaps back to it; between the circles an error is detected but not correctable.

multiplexing_access.caption: Several users share one channel's time–frequency plane. FDM gives each user its own frequency band all the time; TDM gives each user the whole band in turn. CDMA overlays everyone using different codes.

wireless_channels_fading.caption: Received power falls as 10·n·log₁₀(distance); free space has n = 2 but walls and ground push n to 3–4. The link works until power drops below the receiver's sensitivity.

networking_osi_tcpip.caption: Data moves down the layers on the sender, picking up a header at each, and back up on the receiver. Gold: the four TCP/IP layers that the internet actually uses.

magnetic_circuits.caption: A magnetic circuit obeys the same rule as an electric one: mmf = N·I = Φ·ℜ. An air gap adds a large reluctance, so for the same current the flux is far lower and the core stays out of saturation.

power_transformers.caption: Iron loss is fixed while copper loss grows as load². Efficiency peaks where the two are equal, at load √(P_fe/P_cu), so grid transformers are sized to run near that point.

dc_machines.caption: A DC motor's torque falls linearly with speed because its back-EMF E = kω opposes the supply. The operating point is where this line meets the load torque.

induction_motor.caption: An induction motor's rotor must slip behind the rotating field to get any torque. Torque peaks at the breakdown slip, then falls toward standstill (slip 1); normal running is on the steep left part.

synchronous_machines.caption: The rotor stays locked to the grid's rotating field, lagging by the load angle δ. Power rises with sinδ up to 90°; beyond that the machine loses synchronism.

power_generation.caption: Most generation is heat to motion to electricity. Each stage loses energy, and the turbine's thermodynamic limit loses the most, so only about a third of coal's energy reaches the grid.

transmission_distribution.caption: For a given power, current falls as 1/V and I²R loss as 1/V². Raising the voltage fourfold cuts the loss sixteenfold, which is why long lines run at hundreds of kilovolts.

per_unit_system.caption: Per-unit quantities divide by a base, so a 345 kV line and a 13.8 kV generator can share one equation. Change the base and the same ohmic impedance becomes a different per-unit number.

power_flow_analysis.caption: Voltage at a load falls as it draws more power, down to a nose beyond which no solution exists: voltage collapse. A longer, more reactive line (bigger X) has its nose much earlier.

fault_analysis.caption: A short circuit current is a sine plus a decaying DC offset set by the X/R ratio and the instant the fault starts. The first peak can reach nearly twice the steady value, which breakers must withstand.

protection_relays_breakers.caption: An inverse-time relay trips fast for big faults and slowly for small overloads. Setting the upstream relay slower than the downstream one means only the nearest breaker trips: coordination.

grid_renewables_smart.caption: Solar covers the midday peak but not the evening one, carving a 'duck curve' in what other plants must supply. The steep evening ramp is why storage and flexible demand matter.

rectifiers_inverters.caption: A bridge rectifier flips the negative half-cycles; a capacitor then holds the voltage between peaks. A bigger RC (τ, in mains cycles) gives smoother DC. An inverter runs the same idea in reverse.

buck_converter_node.caption: A switch chops 12 V into pulses and an inductor averages them to V_out = D·V_in. The inductor current ramps up while the switch is on and down while it is off; a bigger L shrinks the ripple.

boost_buckboost.caption: A boost converter steps voltage up by 1/(1−D). Real inductor resistance (r) makes the gain collapse at high duty cycle, so practical converters stay below about 0.8.

smps_switching_supplies.caption: A switching supply rectifies the mains, chops it at high frequency through a small transformer, rectifies again and filters. Feedback to the PWM controller adjusts the duty cycle to hold the output steady.

motor_drives.caption: Constant volts-per-hertz control keeps the motor's magnetic flux, and so its torque, constant up to the base frequency. Above it the voltage is maxed out and torque falls ('field weakening').

power_semiconductors.caption: A switch that blocks more voltage needs a thicker, more lightly doped region, so its on-resistance rises roughly as V^2.5. SiC and GaN tolerate far stronger fields and beat silicon's theoretical limit by orders of magnitude.

oscilloscope.caption: An oscilloscope plots voltage against time on a grid of 10 × 8 divisions. Turn the timebase to see more or fewer cycles and the volts/div knob to fill the screen without clipping.

multimeter.caption: A voltmeter is a resistor in parallel with the circuit. When the source resistance is comparable to the meter's input resistance, the reading falls below the true voltage: loading error.

function_generator.caption: A function generator makes sine, square, triangle and sawtooth waves of chosen frequency, amplitude and offset. The spectrum shows why a square wave sounds harsher: it carries odd harmonics.

bench_power_supply.caption: A bench supply holds the set voltage (constant voltage) until the load tries to draw more than the current limit; then it holds the current instead (constant current) and the voltage drops. The dot is where supply and load meet.

logic_analyzer.caption: A logic analyzer records many digital lines at once. Here a serial byte is clocked out LSB first; the gold dots mark where each bit is sampled (rising clock edge). Change the byte and read the waveform.

spectrum_analyzer.caption: A spectrum analyzer shows power versus frequency in dB. A 10 MHz carrier has weak harmonics at 20 and 30 MHz. A narrower resolution bandwidth sharpens peaks and lowers the noise floor, but sweeps more slowly.

breadboarding.caption: Inside a breadboard the five holes of each column strip are connected, and the two halves are separate across the centre gap. Pick a column and half to see which holes share a node.

soldering.caption: Solder only flows once the joint itself is above its melting point (217 °C for lead-free). A bigger pad or ground plane (larger time constant) takes longer to heat, so a hotter iron or more patience is needed.

troubleshooting.caption: Troubleshoot methodically: start with power, then trace signals, and halve the circuit to isolate the fault. After the fix, verify; if it still fails, go back to the symptom.

pcb_design.caption: A board starts as a schematic, becomes a netlist of connections, then components are placed and traces routed. Design-rule checks catch errors before Gerber files go to the fab.

lab_reports_data.caption: Plot measured points with a fitted line and quantify the fit. Adjust slope and intercept by hand to minimise the sum of squared residuals; least squares finds the exact best line.

measurement_error.caption: Repeated readings scatter around the true value with spread σ. Averaging N of them shrinks the uncertainty of the mean to σ/√N, so four times the readings halve the error.

lab_electrical_safety.caption: Current, not voltage, hurts, and a few tens of milliamps across the chest can be fatal. Body resistance sets the current: wet skin can be a hundred times worse than dry. The pink bar is your chosen case.

rf_amplifiers.caption: An RF amplifier is linear only until it nears its saturation power. The 1 dB compression point P1dB, where gain has dropped by 1 dB, marks the top of its useful range.

s_parameters_rf.caption: S-parameters are ratios of waves at the ports: S21 is what gets through and S11 what bounces back. For a lossless bandpass filter the two always share the incident power, |S11|² + |S21|² = 1.

rf_mixers_filters.caption: A mixer multiplies the RF input by a local oscillator, producing sum and difference frequencies. The difference |f_RF − f_LO| is the intermediate frequency (IF) that a filter then selects.

fns.label: gate delay (norm. to 1 V at V_T = 0.3 V)

vlsi_digital_cmos.caption: Dynamic energy per switch grows as V², while delay grows rapidly as the supply approaches the threshold. Chip designers trade the two by lowering voltage when speed is not needed.

vlsi_analog_ic.caption: A differential pair steers its tail current Iss toward whichever input is higher. It is linear only for small differences; emitter or source degeneration (g) trades gain for a wider linear range.

ic_layout_verification.caption: A layout is drawn masks: green diffusion, red polysilicon gate, blue contacts. A transistor forms where poly crosses diffusion. Design-rule checks flag any width below the process minimum (0.1 µm here).

fiber_optics_photonics.caption: Light stays in the glass core by total internal reflection. Only rays entering within the acceptance angle (sinθ ≤ NA = √(n₁²−n₂²)) are guided; steeper ones leak into the cladding and are lost.

photonic_integrated_circuits.caption: A Mach–Zehnder modulator splits light, shifts the phase in one arm with a voltage, and recombines it. Interference turns the phase shift into brightness; V_π is the voltage for a full on-off swing.

wireless_5g6g.caption: Peak rate is bandwidth × spectral efficiency × spatial layers. 5G gets its speed mainly from much wider channels (mmWave) and more MIMO layers, not from cleverer modulation.

mimo_beamforming.caption: With N antennas at each end the channel splits into N parallel streams, so capacity grows about N-fold with no extra bandwidth or power (ideal case, equal channel gains).

radar_systems.caption: Radar measures the delay τ = 2R/c between sending a pulse and hearing its echo: every kilometre adds 6.7 µs. The Doppler shift f_d = 2v/λ of the echo gives the target's speed.

robotics_mechatronics.caption: A two-link robot arm: each joint angle moves the end effector. Forward kinematics gives its position, x = L₁cosθ₁ + L₂cos(θ₁+θ₂); the controller solves the reverse problem.

machine_learning_engineers.caption: Training is gradient descent: step downhill on the loss, w ← w − η·dL/dw. A small learning rate crawls, a good one converges, and one above 1 overshoots and diverges. Watch the dot.

neural_accelerator_hw.caption: A systolic array: inputs flow in from the left and weights from the top, and each multiply-accumulate (MAC) cell passes data on to its neighbours. Thousands of MACs work in lock-step on matrix multiplication.

image_video_processing.caption: A blurred disc (left) and the edges found by differentiating it (right, m = 1). Edge detectors respond where intensity changes quickly; more blur (σ) means weaker, wider edges.

biomedical_instrumentation.caption: An ECG records the heart's electrical cycle: P wave, QRS spike, T wave. Mains interference (60 Hz) can swamp it, which is why instrumentation amplifiers reject common-mode noise.

medical_devices.caption: A demand pacemaker senses the heart's own signal and only fires a pulse if no beat arrives in time. Sensing, timing and stimulation form a closed loop with the tissue.

solar_pv_systems.caption: Panels make DC, a maximum-power-point tracker keeps them at their best voltage, and an inverter turns it into AC for the house or grid. Daily energy = size × sun hours × performance ratio.

wind_energy_systems.caption: Wind power grows with v³, so doubling wind speed gives eight times the power, until the turbine caps it at its rating by pitching the blades. Bigger rotors catch more wind at every speed.

battery_storage_systems.caption: A cell's voltage falls as it empties, and falls further when discharged fast because current flows through its internal resistance. Higher C-rates deliver less usable energy before reaching the cut-off.

params.label: current angle γ from d axis

ev_motor_control.caption: Field-oriented control views the motor from the rotating rotor frame (d, q). The stator current is steered relative to the d axis; the q-axis part makes torque. Raise γ and the torque component grows.

nanotech_mems.caption: A MEMS accelerometer is a proof mass on springs between capacitor plates. Acceleration moves the mass, one gap shrinks and the other grows, and the capacitance difference ΔC/C ≈ Δd/d measures it.

quantum_computing_hardware.caption: Driving a qubit makes it oscillate between |0⟩ and |1⟩ (Rabi oscillation). Decoherence damps the oscillation over the coherence time T₂, which limits how many operations fit before the information is lost.

computer_networks_iot.caption: Many tiny low-power sensors talk by radio to a gateway, which forwards their data over the internet to cloud services and apps. Billions of such nodes form the Internet of Things.

hardware_security.caption: A chain of trust: immutable ROM code verifies the bootloader's signature, which verifies the kernel, and so on. A tampered stage fails its check and the device refuses to start it.

smartphone.caption: A phone is a small computer: the SoC at the centre talks to memory, the screen, camera, sensors and radios, while the PMIC turns the battery into every voltage they need.

phone_display.caption: An OLED pixel is a stack of thin organic layers: electrons and holes injected from the electrodes meet in the emissive layer and release photons. The drive current, set by the TFT beneath, sets the brightness.

phone_touchscreen.caption: Under the glass, drive electrodes (gold) cross sense electrodes (blue); a fingertip steals some of the field at the crossings below it. The map shows the capacitance drop the controller sees; move the finger.

phone_battery.caption: Lithium-ion cells charge in two phases: constant current until about 4.2 V, then constant voltage while the current tapers away. A higher charge rate shortens the first phase but not the taper.

phone_pcb.caption: A phone board is stacked layers of copper and glass-epoxy. A fast trace over a ground plane is a transmission line whose impedance depends on its width w and height h above ground; boards are designed for 50 Ω.

phone_camera.caption: A lens focuses light from an object to an image at distance v where 1/u + 1/v = 1/f. Move the sensor away from that plane and each point smears into a blur circle; autofocus slides the lens until the blur vanishes.

phone_speaker.caption: A phone speaker is a tiny mass on a spring, so it rolls off at 12 dB per octave below its resonance f₀. That is why phones sound thin at low notes; resonance Q adds a bump near f₀.

phone_antenna.caption: An antenna works well where its reflection S11 dips. A metal strip a quarter-wavelength long resonates at f = c/4L, so a 30 mm frame segment suits 2.5 GHz; a longer one tunes lower.

shapes.text: 24 pins, reversible: row A and row B mirror each other

phone_charger_port.caption: The USB-C plug has 24 pins in two mirrored rows so it fits either way up. Four carry power (red), two CC pins negotiate the voltage, and the rest carry data. Pick a power-delivery level below.

phone_vibration_motor.caption: A linear resonant actuator shakes a mass on a spring with a coil. It moves most when driven at its resonance f₀, so haptic drivers lock onto that frequency; a higher Q rings longer after the pulse.

phone_soc.caption: A system-on-chip puts the processor, graphics, AI engine, image processor and modem on one die, linked by an on-chip interconnect to a shared memory controller.

phone_ram.caption: A DRAM bit is charge on a tiny capacitor that leaks away. Every row is refreshed periodically; if the refresh interval is longer than the cell can hold its charge above the sense limit, the bit is lost.

phone_flash.caption: A flash cell stores bits as trapped charge, read as a threshold voltage. Each extra bit per cell halves the spacing between states; as cells wear, the peaks widen (σ) and overlap, causing read errors.

phone_pmic.caption: A linear regulator burns the difference between input and output as heat, so efficiency is just Vout/Vin. A buck converter switches energy through an inductor and stays near 90 %, which is why the PMIC uses bucks for the big rails.

phone_rf_frontend.caption: The front-end keeps the radio's strong transmit signal out of its own sensitive receiver: filters pick the band, a switch shares the antenna, the LNA amplifies weak signals and the PA boosts the outgoing one.

phone_modem.caption: The modem turns bits into an OFDM radio waveform (top row) and, on the way back, recovers bits from the received waveform by reversing each step (bottom row).

phone_wifi_bt.caption: Wi-Fi sits on one 20 MHz channel while Bluetooth hops among 79 1 MHz channels several times a second. Pick Wi-Fi channels 1, 6 or 11 to avoid overlapping neighbours.

phone_sensors.caption: An accelerometer measures gravity along the phone's own axes. Tilt the phone and gravity (red) splits into two components (gold, green); software turns them back into the tilt angle with atan2.

phone_passives.caption: A real capacitor also has parasitic inductance (ESL). Its impedance falls like 1/ωC, bottoms out at the self-resonant frequency, then rises like an inductor, so a 100 nF part stops decoupling above about 20 MHz.

phone_crystal_osc.caption: A quartz crystal behaves like a very high-Q LC circuit: its reactance crosses zero at the series resonance (here 32 768 Hz) and again at the slightly higher parallel resonance. An oscillator locks onto the narrow region between.

soc_cpu_cluster.caption: Power grows roughly as f³ (voltage must rise with frequency). Small cores deliver most performance per watt but top out early; big cores keep scaling but cost much more power. A cluster mixes both.

soc_gpu.caption: A GPU spreads one job over thousands of simple units, but Amdahl's law caps the gain at 1/(1−p), where p is the parallel fraction. Even 1 % serial code limits 4096 cores to about 80×.

soc_npu.caption: Energy per operation (approximate, 45 nm): arithmetic is cheap, moving data is not. An NPU wins by using small integers and keeping data in on-chip memory instead of fetching it from DRAM.

soc_cache.caption: Average memory access time = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty. Even a few percent of misses dominate, because a trip to DRAM costs far more than a cache hit.

soc_memory_controller.caption: DRAM rows must be opened before they can be read. Accesses that hit the already-open row stream data at full speed; a miss pays an activate/precharge delay, so the controller reorders requests to maximise row hits.

soc_isp.caption: The image signal processor turns raw one-colour-per-pixel sensor data into a finished photo through a hardware pipeline of corrections, run on every frame at video rate.

soc_interconnect.caption: Big chips replace one shared bus with a mesh of routers; a message hops from router to router. Watch a packet from the top-left corner reach the bottom-right in four hops.

cpu_core.caption: A core fetches instructions, decodes them, issues them to execution units, accesses the L1 cache when needed and retires results in order. Branch results feed back to the fetch stage.

core_fetch.caption: Fetch sends the program counter to the instruction cache and queues the returned instructions for decode. Normally the PC just advances; the branch predictor redirects it ahead of time.

core_decode.caption: Decode slices the 32-bit instruction word into fields: the opcode picks the operation, the register numbers pick operands, and each field drives control signals or register-file ports.

core_alu.caption: A 4-bit ALU takes two operands and produces a result plus flags. Change A and B and watch the sum wrap around at 16 and the carry flag set.

core_registers.caption: The register file is a small, very fast memory with two read ports and one write port, so an instruction can fetch both operands and store a result in the same cycle.

core_l1_cache.caption: Access time depends on whether the working set fits: L1 holds a few tens of kilobytes at about 4 cycles, then each level further out costs several times more. Programs that fit in L1 run fastest.

core_branch_predictor.caption: A 2-bit saturating counter predicts 'taken' in the two double-ring states. It takes two wrong outcomes in a row to flip the prediction, so a loop's single exit does not spoil it. Watch the input (T = taken, N = not).

core_pipeline.caption: A 5-stage pipeline (Fetch, Decode, Execute, Memory, Write-back) starts a new instruction every cycle, like an assembly line. Add instructions and see the speed-up over finishing each one before starting the next.

logic_adder.caption: A full adder's sum bit is the XOR of its three inputs; the carry-out is 1 when at least two inputs are 1. Toggle A, B and carry-in and check the truth table against 1 + 1 + 1 = 11₂.

logic_gate_nand.caption: NAND is 0 only when both inputs are 1. Because any other gate can be built from NANDs, it is the universal building block of digital chips.

cmos_inverter.caption: In a CMOS inverter one transistor is always off, so it draws almost no current when idle and swings rail to rail. The steepness of the transition (gain g) sets noise margin; each switch costs energy C·V².

finfet_transistor.caption: In a FinFET the channel is a thin vertical fin and the gate wraps it on three sides, so it controls the channel far better than a flat gate. A taller fin adds more channel width in the same footprint.

silicon_channel.caption: The inversion layer is only a few nanometres thick: electrons are squeezed against the oxide by the gate field. A stronger field (more carriers per area Ns) pulls the electrons even closer to the interface.

usb_c_charger.caption: The charger rectifies mains, chops it at high frequency through a small flyback transformer, rectifies and trims the output. A feedback path across the isolation barrier tells it what voltage the phone asked for.

rectifier_bridge.caption: Four diodes always steer current the same way through the load, turning AC into pulsating DC. A bulk capacitor fills the gaps between peaks; a bigger C or lighter load leaves less ripple.

flyback_transformer.caption: A flyback transformer is really a coupled inductor: while the switch is on the primary stores energy; when it turns off, the stored energy is released through the secondary. Turns ratio n sets the output voltage Vo = Vr/n.

switching_mosfet.caption: While a MOSFET turns on, current rises and voltage falls over tr + tf, and their overlap (the gold area) is lost as heat every cycle. Faster switching, or GaN/SiC devices, shrink the area and the loss.

feedback_optocoupler.caption: An optocoupler passes the error signal across the isolation barrier as light: the LED current sets the phototransistor current by the current-transfer ratio (CTR). CTR falls as the LED ages, which the feedback loop must tolerate.

buck_converter.caption: The charger's last stage steps 20 V down to whatever the phone requests (5, 9, 15 V...) by changing the duty cycle D = Vout/Vin. The inductor current's ripple shrinks as inductance or switching speed rises.

electric_power_grid.caption: Supply and demand must balance every instant; the spinning mass of generators (inertia H) is the buffer. If a plant trips, frequency falls, and more inertia makes it fall slower, buying time for other plants to respond.

power_plant.ylabel: % of input energy delivered as electricity
power_plant.caption: Energy conversion efficiency differs widely by source: heat engines are limited by thermodynamics, while hydro and wind convert motion directly. Typical values.

generator.caption: As the rotor's magnetic poles sweep past three coils spaced 120° apart, each coil produces an AC voltage; frequency is f = rpm × poles/120. Faster rotation raises both frequency and amplitude.

step_up_transformer.caption: The same power leaves the transformer at k times the voltage and 1/k the current. Because line loss is I²R, raising the voltage twenty-fold cuts the loss four-hundred-fold.

transmission_line.caption: Overhead conductors hang in a catenary between towers. More tension (larger a) gives less sag; in summer heat the wire lengthens and sags toward the ground, which limits how much current the line may carry.

substation.caption: A substation switches and transforms power. Disconnect switches isolate equipment for maintenance, breakers interrupt fault current, the transformer changes voltage and a bus splits power to several feeders.

distribution_transformer.caption: The last step-down: a transformer on the pole cuts the distribution voltage to 240 V with a centre-tapped secondary. Each half gives 120 V for outlets; both together give 240 V for ovens and dryers.

wall_outlet.caption: The 'voltage' quoted for an outlet is the RMS value; the real peak is √2 times larger. The waveform repeats 50 or 60 times a second, and 120 V RMS does the same heating as 120 V DC.

how_a_phone_charges.caption: AC is converted to DC by the charger, the phone and charger agree a voltage over USB-C, and the charge IC converts it to the right current for the cell. Faster charging is mostly just higher voltage.

how_a_transistor_switches.caption: Raise the gate voltage above the threshold and electrons are drawn under the gate, forming a conducting channel between source and drain: the transistor turns on. Below it, no channel, no current.

instruction_execution.caption: Every instruction, such as ADD x3, x1, x2, goes through the same cycle: look up where it is, fetch it, decode it, execute it, touch memory if needed and write the result. Then the PC moves on.

how_wifi_sends_data.caption: Wi-Fi turns bits into an OFDM radio signal: error-coding, mapping to constellation points, an inverse FFT, conversion to analogue, mixing up to 5 GHz and amplification. The receiver undoes each step.

how_a_photo_is_taken.caption: The lens focuses light, a colour filter lets each pixel see red, green or blue, photodiodes turn photons into electrons, and an ADC and image processor assemble the picture. More photons mean a cleaner image.

chip_fabrication.caption: A wafer goes through the same cycle many times, depositing a layer, coating resist, exposing a pattern, etching and doping, to build transistors and wiring layer by layer. Then it is cut into chips and packaged.

power_grid_delivery.caption: Power is stepped up for efficient long-distance transport, then stepped down in stages to the outlet. The higher the transmission voltage, the smaller the I²R loss on the line.

how_touchscreen_senses.caption: The controller sends a signal along each drive row and measures what arrives on each sense column. A finger near a crossing absorbs some field, so the mutual capacitance drops; the controller finds the biggest drop.
